email_subject: Application - Marketing Associate, Clinical Education (Peripheral Vascular, EMEA)
email_body:
Dear Hiring Team,

I would like to apply for the Marketing Associate, Clinical Education role in Stryker's Peripheral Vascular division.

My work sits where content, web and analytics meet. At Episto I write and publish SEO content for client sites, manage their WordPress CMS and keep existing pages current. One project is a pharmacists' association site, where I maintain a consistent layout across roughly 600 member profile pages - healthcare-adjacent work where structure and terminology have to be right. Earlier, as a front-end developer at ViviDoctor in Belgium, I built features for a healthcare web application.

What draws me to this role is the chance to learn a therapy area properly before writing about it, and the variety: clinical content, sales enablement, events and field support. I'm fluent in English, comfortable working across markets and cultures, and happy to travel for the 60% field component.

I'd welcome a conversation.

Kind regards,
Baver Ok

cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Stryker's Marketing Associate role in Clinical Education asks for someone who can turn dense material into something a sales team or a physician will actually use. That is the work I have been doing since 2024, just with different subject matter: I write, structure and publish content, then check with data whether it landed.

At Episto I handle on-page SEO, keyword research and SEO content for client websites, and manage their CMS - publishing pages, blog posts and media in WordPress, and keeping existing content current. One ongoing project is a pharmacists' association site, majistraleczacilari.org.tr, where I maintain a consistent layout across roughly 600 member profile pages. It taught me how closely healthcare-adjacent audiences read structure and terminology. Before that, as a front-end developer at ViviDoctor in Belgium, I built and optimized features for a healthcare web application, so clinical context is not unfamiliar ground.

What I would bring to Peripheral Vascular: careful management of projects to a deadline, clear written and spoken English, and enough technical fluency to work with structured data, analytics tools (Google Analytics, Search Console, Semrush, Ahrefs) and AI tools that speed up research and content production. I work well alone and with others - most of my current work is remote and cross-border, with stakeholders in different markets.

I will be honest that formal clinical education and congress logistics would be new to me, and that is part of the appeal. The familiarization phase described in the posting is exactly how I prefer to start: learning the disease states, guidelines and clinical data before producing anything. I am ready to travel for field initiatives and to support events where I can add value.

I would like to discuss how my content, web and analytics background could support your EMEA education programs.

Kind regards,
Baver Ok
